title: RV There Yet?
genre: Co-op physics driving / comedy adventure ('friendslop' party co-op, 1–4 players, proximity voice chat)
release_date: 2025-10-21 (PC/Steam); Xbox Series X|S, Xbox PC, Cloud + Game Pass day one 2026-06-30
developer: Nuggets Entertainment (Skövde, Sweden; co-founders Tim Badylak (CEO) and Kristoffer Andersson)
team_size: 4 developers built the game while the rest of the studio was on holiday [CONFIRMED – developers via Automaton, 2026-06-25, reporting a GamesIndustry.biz/Nordic Game 2026 interview]. Studio total ~5 [ESTIMATE – a review calls it a 'five-person studio'; not verified]
developer_background: Co-founders are ex-Coffee Stain (Skövde games cluster). The team had worked together for ~4.5 years on their main project, the farming/survival sim 'Among the Wild' (announced 2024, still in development); burnt out, they took a short break to make RV There Yet? as an extended game jam with a fixed deadline. It is the studio's first released game (debut project)
platforms_and_store_links: Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3949040/RV_There_Yet/ ; Xbox Series X|S / Xbox PC / Game Pass (from 2026-06-30) ; no PlayStation/Switch found
business_model: Premium ~$8 (cheap impulse buy, frequent 10–40% discounts); free content updates (snow map/'vodka' update Dec 2025, language patch 2026); Xbox Game Pass deal (terms undisclosed)
price_usd: ~$8 (US list, likely $7.99) [CONFIRMED-ish – GameDiscoverCo and Notebookcheck both cite '$8'; UK £6.69 per Game Developer; exact US cent price not verified]
units_or_downloads: 1,000,000 in 4 days (2025-10-26) [CONFIRMED – dev, via Automaton]; 1,288,515 by 2025-10-26/27, i.e. ~1.3M in week 1 [CONFIRMED – community manager Jace Varlet YouTube video, via Game Developer/Insider Gaming]; 2.5M+ within ~2 weeks of launch [CONFIRMED – CEO Tim Badylak LinkedIn]; 3.7M in month 1 [ESTIMATE/reported – GameDiscoverCo]; 4.5M+ by ~2025-12-17 (unplanned content update) [CONFIRMED – Nuggets via PC Gamer]. Current Steam: ~5.3–7.1M (Oct 2026) [ESTIMATE – Boxleiter 88.5k reviews × 60–80 (mega-viral friendslop)]; Gamalytic 7.3M (range 4.6–10M) [ESTIMATE]; Raijin 2.1M (Aug 2026) [ESTIMATE – clearly too low vs confirmed 4.5M]. Xbox/Game Pass numbers: no data
peak_concurrent_players: ~100,000 all-time Steam peak on 2025-10-25 [ESTIMATE – Steambase 100,002; Raijin 99,803; dev reported ~100k]. 35,000+ within 2 days of launch (2025-10-23, Automaton). May 2026 monthly peak ~8,448; ~2.4k in-game on 2026-08-31 [Raijin/Steambase]
steam_reviews: ~84,000–88,500 total, ~90% positive, 'Very Positive' (Aug–Oct 2026) [Raijin 83,930 at 2026-08-31; Gamalytic 88.5k at 90%]; English-only ~31,800 at 89% (store snapshot)
implied_review_multiplier: ≥ ~51: confirmed 4.5M units (Dec 2025) ÷ ~88.5k reviews (Oct 2026) – a lower bound because sales kept growing after Dec 2025. Review count at the Dec 2025 milestone: no data. Gamalytic's model implies ~82 (7.3M ÷ 88.5k). Consistent with spec's 60–100+ range for viral friendslop at a sub-$10 price
gross_revenue: Confirmed-units basis: 4.5M × $8 × 0.75 ≈ $27M by Dec 2025 [ESTIMATE – spec method]. Current (Oct 2026): ~6M (mid of 5.3–7.1M) × $8 × 0.75 ≈ $36M [ESTIMATE]. Trackers: Gamalytic $45.4M (range $28.7M–$62.1M) [ESTIMATE]; Raijin $14M (Aug 2026) [ESTIMATE – inconsistent with confirmed units, discarded]
net_revenue: ≈ $24.6M on $36M gross [ESTIMATE – Steam tiered cut: 30% of first $10M ($3M) + 25% of next $26M ($6.5M) = $9.5M; ($36M − $9.5M) × 0.93]. On the confirmed-units basis ($27M gross): ≈ $18.4M. Self-published, so all net goes to the studio. Plus undisclosed Xbox Game Pass fee
production_cost: ≈ $54k [ESTIMATE – 4 people × ~2.25 months (1 week prototype + ~8 weeks) × $6k/month W. Europe lean indie]; at Swedish fully-loaded salaries (~$8–10k/mo with employer taxes) ≈ $70–90k. Excludes 4.5 years of shared tech/experience from Among the Wild. No marketing spend disclosed (appears organic)
development_time: ~9 weeks: core fixed in 1 week, then ~8 weeks to launch [CONFIRMED – devs via Automaton/GamesIndustry.biz]; CEO: launched 'just eight weeks after development began' [CONFIRMED – Tim Badylak LinkedIn]. Press variously reports '3 months' and 'game-jam project in summer 2025' (Icy Veins, Wikipedia)
why_popular: Dead-simple premise everyone gets from one clip: you and up to 3 friends must drive a clunky RV home through a hostile valley – no roads, steep cliffs, rivers, a bear – using physics, a winch and teamwork; one person drives, others push, winch and argue. Proximity voice chat + ragdoll physics turn every failure into a funny shareable moment. $8 impulse price makes 4-packs easy. Arrived at the peak of the 2025 'friendslop' wave (Peak, R.E.P.O., Lethal Company lineage) right before Halloween/autumn group-play season. Low-poly comedic 'dads on a road trip' vibe, beer/smoking gags. Steam algorithm boost (#3 global top seller in week 1)
marketing_channels: Organic virality: streamer and YouTube/Twitch clips of RVs plunging off cliffs (Icy Veins) | Steam front-page/top-sellers momentum (#3 global, top 5 weekly chart) | Very high wishlist conversion: GameDiscoverCo noted a 42x follower-to-wishlist ratio (people wishlisting the 'RV chill times' idea) | $8 price point | Community manager YouTube updates with sales numbers (press amplification) | Discord community | Later: Xbox Game Pass launch (June 2026) to re-surface. No evidence of a Next Fest demo, paid ads or a publisher; TikTok role: no data
engine: Unreal Engine [ESTIMATE – Wikipedia infobox; exact version (likely UE5) no data]
art_style: Stylised low-poly/semi-realistic 3D nature valley, cartoony middle-aged characters, physics-driven vehicle; comedic 'dad road trip' tone
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write vehicle controller and winch/rope code, ragdoll setup, lobby/session code, proximity-voice integration (Steam Voice/Vivox/Dissonance), save/checkpoint logic (Claude Code); generate low-poly props, rocks, trees and the RV (Meshy/Tripo + asset packs), character variants, SFX (engine, crashes, voices via ElevenLabs), music (Suno). The content scope is small (one long map + one later map). | AI cannot: make networked vehicle/rope physics feel stable and funny for 4 players (authority, desync, jitter – the main risk), hand-design the route so every obstacle produces cooperative chaos, tune game feel, playtest with real friend groups, or manufacture the viral streamer moment and timing. The original team was 4 experienced devs with ~4.5 years of shared tech; a solo dev with AI is slower on multiplayer physics. Lowered to 3 due to networked physics sync. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 (Netcode for GameObjects/FishNet + Facepunch Steamworks) or Unreal 5 (built-in replication + Steam OnlineSubsystem) or Godot 4 + GodotSteam; Meshy/Tripo + Synty-style packs for 3D; ElevenLabs SFX; Suno music; Steam Playtest for stress tests
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 6–10 weeks, $300–$900 (Claude Pro/Max, 3D gen sub, low-poly asset packs $50–$200, audio gen, $100 Steam Direct) – 2–4 player Steam-lobby co-op, one vehicle, winch, one short valley route
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 3–6 months, $3,000–$12,000 (AI tool subs ~$100–$300/mo, asset packs, freelance 3D/animation polish $1–5k, networking/QA help, playtests, trailer, streamer key outreach). Excludes developer's own living costs

data_conflicts: Week-1 sales: 1.3M (dev CM, 2025-10-26/27) vs a report of '2.5M in first week' – the CEO's LinkedIn actually says 2.5M within two weeks; used that. A gamedev.net/GamesIndustry syndication said '2M units in eight days' – consistent with the trajectory. Dev time: '8 weeks' (CEO), '1 week + ~8 weeks' (Automaton), '3 months' (Icy Veins) – used ~9 weeks. Team: 4 devs built it (dev interview) vs 'five-person studio' (review) – 4 used for the game. Steam units now: Raijin 2.1M (contradicts confirmed 4.5M, discarded) vs Gamalytic 7.3M vs Boxleiter 5.3–7.1M – reported a range. Gross: Raijin $14M vs Gamalytic $45.4M vs own $27–36M. Xbox Game Pass date: Pure Xbox metadata May 2026 vs Xbox Wire 2026-06-30 – used Xbox Wire. Exact US price ($7.99 vs $8.99) not verified; GameDiscoverCo and Notebookcheck both say '$8'
notes: Probably the best cost-to-revenue ratio in the dataset: ~9 weeks × 4 people (~$50–90k) → $25M+ net, self-published. The lesson: a funny, physics-driven co-op premise that reads in a 10-second clip, priced under $10, released into an active trend (friendslop) can explode with zero marketing budget. The devs treated it as a short break from their 'real' game, so the scope was ruthlessly small (1 map at launch). Their 4.5 years of working together and existing UE tech made 8-week production possible; a solo dev should expect 2–4x longer, mostly on multiplayer physics. The hit did not lift wishlists for their main game (Among the Wild) much, per Icy Veins – virality attaches to the game, not the studio
